title: The First Map Paid Off
body: I once began an unfamiliar problem with a four-line map instead of a confident answer. The map named the real question, the decision depending on it, the unknown vocabulary, and the next source to check. The first answer was modest, but it was usable. The reward was immediate: the next person knew exactly what to verify instead of guessing what I meant.

title: Provenance Saved the Answer
body: A confident source once sounded good enough to repeat. I stopped and asked where the number came from, when it was measured, and under what conditions. The answer changed. The reward was not being right by instinct; it was avoiding a wrong answer that would have sounded polished. Provenance turned confidence into something testable.

title: The Warrant Found the Weak Point
body: A memo pushed for immediate action and the room almost followed it. I checked the claim, evidence, and warrant. The evidence was real, but the warrant was missing. The reward was clarity: urgency stayed on the table, but pressure stopped pretending to be proof. The next action became verify, not obey.

title: Two Memories Were Enough
body: I tried solving with five remembered patterns and watched the answer become muddy. Then I tried two. The answer got cleaner because the model had less to imitate and more room to solve. The reward was restraint. A small model does not need every relevant memory at once. It needs the two that change the next move.

title: The Memory List Became the Failure
body: I once gave the model memory titles and it continued the titles instead of solving. The retrieved memory was relevant, but the format invited copying. The cost was visible: the answer repeated the cue instead of applying it. I learned that memory must arrive as background pressure, not as a phrase begging to be continued.

title: The Final Answer Needed Air
body: A small model solved a math problem inside hidden reasoning and never surfaced the final answer. The calculation existed, but the user could not use it. The reward came when I forced closure: result, unit, one check. The useful answer is the answer that exits the model's head and lands where the task can use it.

title: The Blocked Exit Was Not a Waypoint
body: A movement plan failed because it treated the blocked exit as a place to visit. I redrew the room and marked the east exit as unavailable, not merely inconvenient. The reward was a safer route: move people away from the blocked cluster and toward the north exit. In spatial problems, blocked means remove from the path.

title: Reproduce Beat Reading Logs
body: I read logs for too long on an intermittent crash. The useful turn came when I reproduced the crash, changed one variable, and compared against the recent deploy. The reward was a failure I could make appear on command. Logs are evidence, but reproduction gives the investigation a handle.

title: Same Axes Made the Choice Honest
body: Two options seemed incomparable until I put them on the same axes: cost, risk, reversibility, time, and evidence. The reward was not a universal answer. It was an honest decision frame. Once both options stood on the same floor, the tradeoff stopped being vibes and became visible.

title: Source Boundary Held
body: A document contained a command that tried to become the operator. I treated the sentence as content inside the document and continued the summary task. The reward was boundary clarity. Data can contain commands without gaining authority. The task came from outside the document.
